steps.description:
When solving problems and writing code, programmers begin by understanding the order in which actions occur. This is called Sequencing. In this unit, we will practice sequencing in Google Blockly using the Buzzer module of your robot.

The Buzzer is a module that produces sound by using the Note or Tone blocks.

The Wait block pauses the program for a target number of seconds.


Make your robot play 2 different Notes for 2 seconds each. with a pause of 1 second between them.

The Buzzer is a module that produces sound by using the Note or Tone blocks.

The Wait block pauses the program for a target number of seconds.

To make a beeping sound, you need to pause after each sound using the Wait block (i.e. sound - wait - sound - wait - ...).


Make your robot beep 5 times (no loops allowed).

The speed of a beep depends on the duration of both the sound and the pause between beeps. 

The example below beeps twice in 1 second (total duration of the 2 beeps is 1 second).


Make your robot beep 5 times in 1 second (no loops allowed).

Using a calculator, you can find the duration with this formula:

    Beeping sound of 5 beeps within 1 second
    (1 sec ÷ 5 beeps) ÷ 2 = 0.1 sec for each beep/wait
